title: Somerset County athletes gear up for Ken Lantzy All-Star Classic - NewsBreak
text:
By Adam Ripple ,
1 days ago The 55th installment of the storied 1st Summit Bank Ken Lantzy All-Star Classic is set for 7 p.m., Friday, June 12, at Greater Johnstown's Trojan Stadium.
Somerset County athletes will compete on both the North and South squads following a draft, in which the respective head coaches select their squads.
Berlin Brothersvalley’s Levi Leonard and Seth Kimmel, Conemaugh Township’s D.J. Bambino, Brennan Lohr, Jacob Bartis and Liam Richardson, North Star's Bryson Durst, Somerset’s Colt Hagans, Cole Parry and Carter Dunmyer, as well as Windber’s Nathan Betcher, Cole Mash and Lucas Rummel will represent the South. Bambino will not play due to an injury.
Kimmel is headed to Juniata College, while Durst, a Class 2A all-state defensive back who was tied for a state-high nine interceptions, and Lohr will play at St. Vincent College. Betcher is set to join the St. Francis University football program.
All-state nod North Star's Durst selected to Pa. Football Writers' 2A all-state team
Postseason accolades Meyersdale pair garner Pa. Football Writers' 1A all-state honors
Kimmel, who will play linebacker in the game, is excited for the opportunity to play under the Friday night lights one more time and take in everything the week entails.
"This is great," said Kimmel. "Guys you know and that you've had rivalries with, they are your teammates, now. You get to know them, and they are super fun to be around. I am hoping to get a big win with these guys that I've become friends with. We formed some great relationships already this week."
Richland’s Brandon Bailey guides the South team. His staff includes Marion Center’s Adam Rising, former North Star coach Bob Landis, Richland’s Devon Gates and Tim Ripple, along with Windber’s Frank Tallyen.
Meyersdale’s Lance Jones, Caleb Snyder, Caden Snyder and Landon Ludy will play for the North.
Jones, a Salisbury-Elk Lick student athlete who competes in a co-op with Meyersdale, had a stellar season. He earned Pennsylvania Football Writers' Class 1A all-state honors as an athlete. Jones completed 97 of 171 passes for 1,551 yards 13 touchdowns and 11 interceptions. He also rushed for 370 yards and six touchdowns. Jones racked up 1,921 yards of total offense. Defensively, Jones notched 38 tackles to go along with a team-high six interceptions. Jones will play at St. Francis University.
The North team is coached by Penn Cambria's Jason Grassi. His staff includes Claysburg-Kimmel’s Chuck Kassick, Homer-Center’s Greg Page, Penn Cambria’s Brent Davison and Brandon Nicodemus, as well as Portage’s Marty Slanoc.
Unlike many years' past, the players are not staying in the dorms at UPJ. Rather than going out to lunch and dinner, local businesses are catering food at Forest Hills, where the North is practicing, and Windber, where the South is preparing. The annual dinner banquet, Thursday, is being held at The Willow rather than Sunnehanna County Club.
While the game and week leading up to the Ken Lantzy All-Star Classic has changed and evolved over the years, the lore is still the same. The game honors Lantzy, a former Cambria Heights football player who sustained an injury in 1970 that would confine him to a wheelchair for the rest of his life.
Adam Ripple is the Daily American sports editor. He can be reached at 814-444-5926. Follow him on X @ARipple_DAsport. Follow Daily American Sports on Facebook and @dailyamericanmedia on Instagram.
